title: Stack buffer overflow in curl_easy_setopt_safe() via long redirect URL (RCE)
body:
## Summary
A stack-based buffer overflow in `curl_easy_setopt_safe()` allows remote code execution when libcurl follows a redirect to a long URL.

## Details
In `lib/easy.c` line 3412, `curl_easy_setopt_safe()` copies the redirect URL into a fixed 1024-byte stack buffer with `strcpy()` without validating its length. Because `CURLOPT_FOLLOWLOCATION` makes libcurl copy the `Location:` header value, a malicious server fully controls the overflow (CWE-121).

The vulnerable helper `Curl_follow_redirect_copy()` in `lib/transfer_safe.c` is also affected.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Run a server that answers with `Location: http://` followed by 5000 `A` characters.
2. `curl -L http://attacker.example/`

## ASan output
```
==31337==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow on address 0x7ffd5c3a1e40
WRITE of size 5012 at 0x7ffd5c3a1e40 thread T0
    #0 0x55d0c1 in curl_easy_setopt_safe lib/easy.c:3412:5
    #1 0x55d2f7 in Curl_follow_redirect_copy lib/transfer_safe.c:88:3
    #2 0x55e010 in Curl_follow lib/transfer.c:1501:9
```

## Impact
Remote code execution in every application using libcurl 8.4.0 with redirects enabled.
